report.tagline: America's biggest food delivery app, now also delivering groceries and retail, and owner of Deliveroo.
report.simpleSummary: You open DoorDash, pick a restaurant, and a driver called a Dasher brings your food in about 30 to 40 minutes. You pay for the food plus delivery and service fees and a tip. Restaurants pay DoorDash a cut of each order. It now also delivers groceries, pharmacy items and pet food, owns the UK's Deliveroo, and in October 2026 agreed to buy Instacart.

overview.whatItDoes: DoorDash is a three-sided marketplace: it connects customers, local merchants (restaurants and stores) and Dashers (gig drivers). It started in 2013 at Stanford as PaloAltoDelivery. It won the US by going to suburbs and smaller cities that rivals ignored, and it now has roughly two-thirds of US food delivery (estimate). It also sells software and delivery services to restaurants and runs ads for brands.
howItWorks: A customer orders in the DoorDash app and sees fees before paying.
The restaurant gets the order on a tablet and starts cooking.
DoorDash's dispatch system offers the delivery to a nearby Dasher, timed to arrive as the food is ready.
The Dasher picks up and delivers; the customer tracks them live.
DoorDash pays the restaurant minus its commission and pays the Dasher a base amount plus 100% of tips.
DashPass members pay a monthly fee for $0 delivery and lower service fees on eligible orders.
overview.valueProposition: Customers get almost any local restaurant or store delivered fast. Restaurants get extra orders without hiring drivers. Dashers get flexible work.

coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Earns money even when customers order outside the app.

businessModel.summary: DoorDash keeps about 13.6% of order value. That money comes from restaurant commissions, customer delivery and service fees, DashPass fees and ads. Most of the rest goes to merchants and Dashers.

revenueStreams.detail: About 15% to 30% of the food price, depending on the plan.
Delivery fee, service fee and small order fee.
$9.99 a month or $96 a year in the US.
Sponsored listings and promotions bought by restaurants and consumer brands.
Drive (delivery for others), Storefront and software for restaurants.

businessModel.pricing: Customers pay menu price plus a delivery fee (often $0 to $5), a service fee (often around 15% of the subtotal) and an optional tip. DashPass costs $9.99 a month. Restaurants choose plans with about 15%, 25% or 30% commission.
costDrivers: Refunds and credits for wrong or missing orders
Marketing and promotions ($765 million in Q3 2026)
Engineering and technology ($499 million R&D in Q3 2026)
New bets: autonomous delivery, warehouses, international expansion
Legal and regulatory costs around gig worker pay rules
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a $40 order, total order value with fees and tip is around $50. DoorDash keeps about 13.6%, so roughly $6.80. Out of that it pays support, refunds, payments and part of Dasher pay not covered by fees. Its adjusted EBITDA was 3.1% of GOV in Q3 2026, so it keeps roughly $1.50 of profit before some costs on that order. Profit grows with ads and with batching two orders on one Dasher trip.

howTheyGetUsers: Biggest restaurant selection, especially in suburbs
DashPass free trials and partner bundles (like Chase cards and Lyft)
Expansion into grocery and retail and abroad through Wolt and Deliveroo
whatBringsUsersBack: DashPass: paid members want to use what they paid for
Habit of ordering on set nights
Promotions funded by restaurants and brands
growth.moat: DoorDash has a network effect: more customers attract more restaurants, which attracts more customers, and more orders keep Dashers busy, cutting delivery time and cost. Its density in suburbs means its cost per delivery is lower than rivals'. Paid DashPass members are sticky.

competitors.name: Uber Eats

competitors.howThisProductDiffers: DoorDash leads in suburbs and restaurant selection; Uber wins with users who also ride.

competitors.name: Instacart

competitors.howThisProductDiffers: DoorDash is food-first and growing in grocery; it agreed to buy Instacart in 2026.

competitors.name: Grubhub
competitors.positioning: Older US delivery app, now owned by Wonder.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Grubhub has lost share; strongest in some big cities and campuses.

competitors.name: Amazon

competitors.howThisProductDiffers: DoorDash is local and on-demand; Amazon is the biggest threat in retail delivery.

pmLessons: Go where rivals are not. DoorDash beat bigger players by winning suburbs first, where orders were bigger and competition weaker.
Marketplaces must keep all sides happy. A change that helps customers can hurt Dashers or restaurants, so watch guardrails.
A membership like DashPass turns occasional users into frequent ones.
Ads can make a thin-margin marketplace profitable.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase DashPass sign-ups without hurting profit?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find users who order enough to benefit, target them with savings shown at checkout, and track member order frequency and margin per member.

interviewQuestions.question: Delivery times rose 10% in one city. How do you investigate?
interviewQuestions.hint: Split into restaurant prep time, Dasher wait, travel and assignment. Check Dasher supply, weather and new merchants. Fix the biggest driver.

interviewQuestions.question: Should DoorDash charge customers more or restaurants more?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare price sensitivity on each side, competitor pricing and long-term health. Suggest a test and guardrails.

interviewQuestions.question: What should DoorDash do with Instacart after the deal closes?
interviewQuestions.hint: Think about customers, retailers, shoppers and ads. Integration vs separate brands. Key metrics: grocery orders and retailer retention.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to reduce missing item complaints.
interviewQuestions.hint: Map where items go missing. Ideas: bag sealing, checklists at pickup, photo proof. Track missing item rate and refund cost.
